- "10th week" = calendar weeks from the season's start, Saturday 17 August 1974. Week 1 = 17–23 Aug, Week 2 = 24–30 Aug, ... Week 10 = 19–25 Oct 1974. So the cutoff is: include every First Division league match played on or before Friday 25 October 1974 (inclusive), regardless of how many games each team has played as a result (teams may have unequal games-played counts due to postponements/rearrangements — that's expected and correct under this interpretation, not an error to fix).
- Domain rules already fixed elsewhere (don't re-derive, just be aware): 2 points for a win, 1 for a draw, 0 for a loss; tiebreak order is points, then goal average (goals_for / goals_against, historically — NOT goal difference, which didn't exist as a rule until 1976/77), then goals scored.
- The 22 clubs in the division that season: Derby County, Liverpool, Ipswich Town, Everton, Stoke City, Sheffield United, Middlesbrough, Manchester City, Leeds United, Burnley, Queens Park Rangers, Wolverhampton Wanderers, West Ham United, Coventry City, Newcastle United, Arsenal, Birmingham City, Leicester City, Tottenham Hotspur, Luton Town, Chelsea, Carlisle United.

YOUR TASK (research only — do not write any files, this is read-only data gathering):

1. For each of the 22 clubs, fetch its "1974–75 [Club] F.C. season" Wikipedia article (URL pattern: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1974%E2%80%9375_<Club>_F.C._season — adjust for clubs whose article title differs, e.g. disambiguation). Extract every First Division (league) match with its date, opponent, venue (home/away), and score, for matches dated 17 August 1974 through 25 October 1974 inclusive. Ignore FA Cup / League Cup / friendly matches — league matches only.

2. Since each match involves two clubs, use this to cross-check: the score recorded on the home club's page and the away club's page for the same fixture must agree. Note any discrepancies you find (don't silently resolve them — flag them).

3. Assemble the full list of distinct league matches in this window (there should be roughly 100–115, since 22 teams × up to 10 games ÷ 2 ≈ 110, though some teams may have played fewer or more due to rearranged fixtures — that's expected, not an error).

4. Cross-check overall plausibility against RSSSF's page at https://www.rsssf.org/engpaul/FLA/1974-75.html (which has final-season aggregate stats per team, home/away splits) — e.g., sanity-check that no match you've recorded has a scoreline inconsistent with known aggregate patterns, and that team names match. This is a secondary sanity check only, not a primary source (it only has final standings, not round-by-round).

5. Also independently verify against a *third*, non-Wikipedia source where possible for at least a sample of matches (e.g. try worldfootball.net, 11v11.com, or footballfacts.co.uk — note some sites may block fetches; if a site fails, say so and move to another rather than giving up on cross-verification entirely).

Report back (this is what matters — be thorough and precise, since this data will directly become the graded submission dataset):
- The full compiled match list as a table: date, home_team, away_team, home_goals, away_goals — in chronological order. Use exactly these club names (matching the 22 listed above) for consistency.
- Which Wikipedia article URL you used for each club (so it can be cited as a source).
- Any discrepancies found between a club's home-page and away-page account of the same match, and how (if at all) you resolved them.
- Any matches you could not find/verify, or any club whose season article was missing/structured differently than expected.
- The resulting games-played count per team as of the cutoff (should mostly be 10, but flag any that aren't, with the likely reason e.g. a postponed fixture).
- Confirmation of whether third-party cross-verification (step 5) was actually possible, and what it showed.

Be exhaustive and careful — accuracy matters more than speed here. If you run low on room to fetch all 22 club pages individually, prioritize accuracy over the sanity-check steps, but do not skip any of the 22 clubs' primary match data.
